subject.title: fix(release): harden publication and supply chain

question: Is the single SSH key in `.github/release-allowed-signers` the approved production release trust root, with confirmed operator custody and a recovery path?
rationale: The checkout proves that this PR replaces the existing release procedure with a signer-enforced authorization boundary, but repository history and PR discussion do not establish who controls the corresponding private key or whether all intended release operators can complete the cutover.

options.title: Approve and prove this signer
options.body: Retain the single key only after release owners confirm private-key custody and recovery access and demonstrate a signed-tag release run.

options.title: Expand the approved signer set
options.body: Add the SSH public keys of every authorized release operator and validate that each supported release path verifies correctly.

options.title: Delay the signing cutover
options.body: Preserve the current publication procedure until signer custody, rotation, and operator migration are ready.

recommendation.title: Approve and prove this signer
recommendation.body: Retain the single key only after release owners confirm private-key custody and recovery access and demonstrate a signed-tag release run.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and currently owns the repository's release surface and is the only strong feature-history candidate for confirming the intended signing model.
